title: Redwood Inference — Standard 30-Minute Demo Run of Show (v1)
content:
Purpose
- Give AEs + SEs a repeatable, minute-by-minute plan for a 30-minute Redwood Inference demo.
- Defines who speaks when (AE ↔ SE), what to click/run, and what to do when something goes sideways.

Audience
- Default: App Eng + ML Eng + Platform Lead on the customer side.
- Optional module (narrative-only): Security/IT reviewer.

Prereqs (do these BEFORE the call)
Owner: SE (5–10 min before joining)
1) Confirm demo tenant health
   - Run demo healthcheck (internal): demo tenant healthcheck endpoint/CLI output must be GREEN for:
     - Auth OK
     - Quota OK (no 429 risk)
     - Pinned model available (primary)
     - Fallback model available (secondary)
     - Telemetry ingestion OK (dashboards should populate)
2) Start/confirm synthetic traffic generator
   - Ensure last 15–30 minutes show activity in Console (latency + tokens + errors graphs not empty).
3) Open tabs/windows (keep them ready, not shared yet)
   - Tab A: Redwood Console (Demo Org)
   - Tab B: API key page (ready to show scopes briefly; do not scroll into full key value)
   - Tab C: Demo app (local or hosted) with scenario runner
   - Tab D: Terminal with curl examples (streaming + structured output + tool calling)
   - Tab E: Rollouts/Routing view in Console (pinned route + fallback policy)
   - Backup: PDF deck + 3 screenshots (dashboards, rollout view, audit log)
4) Safety
   - Confirm you’re in DEMO ORG (synthetic data only). Do not open any customer orgs/projects.
   - Hide notifications; close Slack/Email popups.

Call roles
- AE (driver of narrative + discovery + commercial framing): Avery Johnson / Priyom Das / Hannah Schmitt
- SE (technical driver of live product + credibility + Q&A): Markus Klein / SE team

Success criteria (for this 30-min format)
- Customer sees: (1) “Hello world” API that behaves like production (streaming, retries), (2) levers to control cost/latency (batch/cache) with observability, (3) reliability story (fallback), (4) enterprise posture (narrative) without derailing timing.

Minute-by-minute run of show (30:00)

0:00–1:30 — Opening + agenda (AE)
- Script cue: “We’ll do a fast, production-style walkthrough: API → economics/observability → reliability/fallback → quick enterprise/security posture. We’ll leave 5 minutes for Q&A.”
- Confirm timebox: “Do you have the full 30 minutes?”
- Set expectation: “Everything you see is synthetic traffic in a demo tenant; we do this to keep it repeatable and safe.”

1:30–4:00 — 2 discovery questions to tailor emphasis (AE)
Ask ONLY two:
1) “What’s the user-facing latency budget (p50/p95) you care about?”
2) “What are you optimizing for first: cost per 1M tokens, reliability/SLA, or deployment constraints (VPC/on-prem)?”
Handoff cue to SE: “Based on that, Markus will run the API flow and we’ll tune for what you care about.”

4:00–11:00 — Core API demo (SE live)
Goal: Show developer-first API + streaming + structured output + tool calling in ~7 minutes.

Live steps (suggested order)
A) Show the model/route selection quickly (Console, 30–45 sec)
   - Navigate: Console → Projects → DEMO Project (e.g., “demo-core-api”) → Routes
   - Point out:
     - Route name is stable (pinned)
     - Region selection (mention multi-region support)
     - Version pin label (don’t over-explain yet)

B) Streaming chat completion (2–3 min)
   - In terminal or demo app:
     - Run “Scenario 1: Streaming Chat” (scripted runner)
   - Say while it runs:
     - “This is token streaming; you can start rendering immediately.”
     - “We support retries/timeouts; the client SDK handles transient disconnects gracefully.”
   - Optional (only if asked): show minimal code snippet (10–20 lines max).

C) Structured output (2 min)
   - Run “Scenario 2: Structured JSON output” (e.g., support ticket extraction).
   - Emphasize:
     - “We validate schema adherence and surface parse failures clearly.”
     - “This is the difference between a demo and a production integration—predictable outputs.”

D) Tool calling (2 min)
   - Run “Scenario 3: Tool calling” (simple function like “lookup_order_status” or “search_docs”).
   - Emphasize:
     - “Tools + structured output are where apps tend to break. We focus on making this reliable at inference-time.”

AE interjection (10 sec, timed): “So the baseline is straightforward for your team: API + SDKs + production behaviors.”

11:00–19:30 — Production economics + observability (SE live, AE narrates value)
Goal: Show the knobs and the proof (dashboards) without getting stuck in UI.

Live steps
A) Show dashboard: token-level cost + latency breakdown (Console) (2–3 min)
   - Navigate: Console → Observability (or Usage/Cost) → select demo project
   - Callouts:
     - Latency p50/p95
     - Tokens in/out
     - $ cost (synthetic but realistic)
     - Error rate (should be low)
   - Script line: “The dashboard is designed for operators: where time/cost goes per route/model.”

B) Flip one lever: caching OR batching (3–4 min)
Choose based on discovery:
- If cost-sensitive: show caching first
- If latency-sensitive: show batching vs latency trade-off carefully

Option 1: Prefix/KV caching (recommended default)
   - Navigate: Route settings → caching toggle/preset
   - Run “Scenario 4: Repeated prompt set” (same prefix)
   - Show in dashboard (or trace) that:
     - latency drops for subsequent requests
     - cost per request decreases

Option 2: Batching (only if you can show it clearly)
   - Navigate: Route settings → batching preset
   - Run “Scenario 5: Burst traffic (20–50 requests)”
   - Point out:
     - throughput improvement
     - note trade-off: tail latency can increase under batch

C) Trace/error analysis quick glance (2 min)
   - Navigate: Console → Traces (or Requests)
   - Click 1 request
   - Callouts:
     - timeline (queue → compute → stream)
     - retry metadata
     - model version

AE value framing (30–45 sec)
- “This is where teams win on unit economics—without rewriting their whole stack. You get the levers plus the measurement.”

19:30–24:30 — Reliability demo: pinned model + safe fallback (SE live)
Goal: Tell a credible ‘graceful degradation’ story and show the control plane view.

Live steps
A) Show routing/fallback policy (2 min)
   - Navigate: Console → Routes → (demo route) → Routing / Rollouts
   - Callouts:
     - “Pinned primary model version for stability”
     - “Compatible fallback model variant(s)”
     - “Fallback triggers: capacity constraint, model health, region issues (policy-based)”

B) Execute controlled fallback (2–3 min)
   - Run “Scenario 6: Fallback simulation” (uses a safe switch or chaos flag in demo tenant)
   - Show outcome:
     - request still succeeds
     - response includes metadata (e.g., model_used / region)
   - Script line: “The customer experience stays up. You can choose what changes: model, region, or response quality envelope.”

Do NOT overdo:
- Avoid deep kernel/runtime discussions unless asked.
- Avoid claiming ‘zero downtime’—stick to ‘graceful degradation + policy controls’.

24:30–27:00 — Enterprise/security posture (AE leads, SE confirms) (mostly narrative)
Goal: Give procurement/security enough to keep momentum without turning into a security review.

AE script bullets
- “Deployment modes: Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem). Same API + operational tooling.”
- “Security basics: SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption, retention controls, and region/residency options.”
- “We can follow up with the full security FAQ and SOC2 package under NDA.”

SE backup if asked (show only if time permits)
- Show audit log screenshot or Console page (30–60 sec). Do not scroll through noisy logs; point out:
  - key actions are captured (key creation/rotation, role changes, route changes)
  - retention controls are configurable (where applicable)

27:00–30:00 — Wrap + next steps + Q&A (AE)
- Confirm what resonated:
  - “Is the main win here economics, reliability, or deployment flexibility?”
- Propose next step (pick one):
  1) “Technical deep dive on routing + SLOs (45 min)”
  2) “POC scoping call with success metrics (30 min)”
  3) “Security review session (45–60 min) with our security advisor”
- Close: “We’ll send the recap with links to docs, security FAQ, and a sample eval prompt set if you’d like.”

Handoff cues (use these verbatim to avoid talking over each other)
- AE → SE:
  - “Markus, can you show them what this looks like in the API and Console?”
  - “Can you run the economics toggle and then we’ll come back to what it means commercially?”
- SE → AE:
  - “That’s the technical piece; Avery, do you want to translate how customers typically package this?”
  - “I’ll pause there—Avery can cover deployment options and next steps.”

Exact live checklist (SE) — what to click/run
1) Console: confirm project dropdown = demo project (say the name out loud)
2) Routes: open demo route
3) Run demo app Scenario 1 (streaming)
4) Run Scenario 2 (structured output)
5) Run Scenario 3 (tool calling)
6) Console: open cost/latency dashboard (last 30 min)
7) Toggle caching or batching preset
8) Run Scenario 4/5 to show before/after
9) Console: open traces; click 1 request
10) Console: open routing/rollouts view
11) Run fallback simulation scenario; confirm request metadata shows fallback model/region

Standard “if it breaks” playbook (keep calm, do not debug on-call)
- If dashboards are empty:
  1) Switch dashboard time range to “Last 24 hours”
  2) If still empty: run synthetic traffic generator preset (1–2 min)
  3) If still empty: use backup screenshot (DES-611) and continue narrative
- If you hit 429 / quota errors:
  1) Pause live load test scenarios
  2) Switch to single-request scenarios only
  3) Mention “This is exactly why we surface quotas + rate limits clearly”
  4) Use fallback recording/screenshots; after call, follow demo quota runbook
- If model errors / primary unavailable:
  1) Don’t reconfigure on the fly
  2) Use the reliability narrative + show policy view
  3) Run the fallback scenario (if it still works) OR use canned output + screenshot
- If auth/RBAC blocks Console:
  1) Do not fight the login loop
  2) Switch to terminal/API demo + prepared screenshots for Console sections
  3) After call: file INT ticket and rotate credentials

Timeboxing guidance (what to cut first)
- Must keep: streaming + one of (structured output/tool calling) + one observability view + reliability story.
- Cut order if running long:
  1) Tool calling (keep structured output)
  2) Trace deep click-through
  3) Batching (keep caching)
  4) Any security UI (keep narrative only)

Variants (quick swaps)
- Exec/20-minute version:
  - Do: Streaming (2 min) → dashboard proof (4 min) → reliability narrative (3 min) → deployment/security narrative (3 min) → next steps.
- EMEA/data residency emphasis:
  - Add 60–90 sec in enterprise section: region controls, residency posture, Private/VPC option.
- Search/embeddings use case:
  - Replace tool calling with embeddings + rerank scenario (if available in demo app), then show cost dashboard per endpoint.

Notes to presenters
- Keep clicks deliberate; narrate where you’re going before you click.
- Never paste a real API key into chat; if you need to show a key, show scopes and creation flow only.
- Avoid hard numbers unless they are from the approved benchmark set. Use relative improvements (e.g., “notice the drop”) and offer to share detailed benchmarks after the call.

Owner checklist (maintenance)
- Monthly: re-validate that scenario runner outputs match ‘known-good’ expectations.
- After any incident: update the “if it breaks” section with the new failure mode + workaround.
- When the deck/talk track updates: sync naming and module order so AE and SE stay aligned.
